items.title: Strait of Hormuz / Iran escalation
items.detail: US-Iran exchanges continue; Iran says the ceasefire has collapsed and reports intercepting vessels near Hormuz. Brent whipsawed to ~$87.72 after spiking near $91 last week. An oil shock is the single biggest macro swing factor.

items.title: S&P 500 slipped below its 200-day average
items.detail: Index closed 7,443.28 vs a 7,465.82 200-day and has been under its 50-day since 17 Jul. A decisive break would flip the primary trend from up to neutral/down.

items.title: Narrow, rotating leadership
items.detail: The semis index sits ~20% below its late-June peak even after Monday's bounce; leadership has been rotating through energy, banks, healthcare and rails. Breadth, not breakout, is carrying the tape.

items.title: Healthcare earnings headwind
items.detail: Managed care is the only S&P sector with a year-over-year earnings decline as GLP-1 driven utilization lifts medical-loss ratios - a real risk for UNH/ELV/OSCR despite insider buying.

items.title: Fed on hold, but dots still split
items.detail: Funds rate 3.50-3.75%; 28-29 Jul meeting ~80% priced for no change, yet a minority of dots still show a 2026 hike. Sticky energy-led inflation keeps a hawkish tail alive.

items.title: AI-capex concentration
items.detail: A handful of AI names still drive index-level FCF and sentiment. Any single hyperscaler capex guide-down could de-rate the whole complex regardless of individual execution.
